newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin says expects bourse will calm down.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin says expects bourse will calm down.

text.p: French Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin said on Friday that the Socialists have addressed the issues worrying financial markets and he said he expected the stockmarket to calm down after the parliamentary election.
The bourse has lost six percent this week on the Socialists' victory in the first round last Sunday and polls showing them well placed for the runoff this coming Sunday.

"I'm not a stock specialist. I don't have a portfolio of stocks, personally, or bonds, and never did. But I think what the bourse doesn't like is uncertainty. When that uncertainty is lifted, I think it'll calm down," he told radio France Info.

"On a certain number of points that could have worried financial circles ... we have said we could not envisage increasing public spending, and the record level of payroll deductions attained by this government cannot be broken," he said.
"Even if we set conditions for joining a single currency ... we remain fundamentally pro-European," he said.
